messages:
jia: noticed something weird in Console quick preview flow — when I switch workspace via the top selector the quick preview pane sometimes shows runs from the previously-selected org :eyes:

matt: whoa. steps to repro?

jia: 1) open console on workspace A 2) open Run details 3) click workspace selector -> select workspace B 4) click Quick Preview on the run card. sometimes the run list in the quick preview shows rows from A

olivia: can you grab the network tab / request payload? might be a caching header or stale workspace id in the preview request

jia: here's the fetch that returns the preview:
```
GET /api/v1/runs/preview?run_id=abc123&workspace=workspace-b
200 OK
response: { items: [ {id: "run-1", workspace: "workspace-a", ...}, ... ] }
```

jia: note the request param workspace=workspace-b but the payload contains workspace-a items

sara: my first guess: we have a shared KV cache keyed by run_id only, not including workspace. If runs are globally unique in the DB but not scoped in the cache key, preview could return stale cross-tenant results

matt: ugh. that matches a change from last sprint where we memoized run details by id to avoid an extra DB read. cache key was `run:${id}` not `workspace:${ws}:run:${id}`

olivia: do we have any telemetry showing cross-tenant hits? that would be an important audit signal. get a quick filter on request/response pairs for mismatched workspace fields

infra-bot: alert: anomalous-telemetry detected for /api/v1/runs/preview — 1.4% responses with workspace mismatch in last 10m

jia: ok created a small local patch to scope cache keys. patch: `const key = `${workspace}:run:${id}`` — quick test looks good locally

matt: can you open a PR with the change and add a unit test that asserts cache keys include workspace? add a regression-test that simulates two workspaces with same run id mapping (simulate in test DB)

olivia: also add a short migration to invalidate existing cache entries (or bump cache namespace). we should avoid manual invalidation across pods

jia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4112 — includes unit + integration test, and bumps cache namespace v2

sara: question for rollout strategy: do we need a canary? this affects cross-tenant isolation, so safer to deploy via canary to a single region + run synthetic checks

matt: agree. canary to staging->small% prod with synthetic that flips workspace selector fast and asserts no workspace leakage for 1000 iterations

olivia: add an alert rule: if infra-bot workspace-mismatch rate > 0.1% over 5m then rollback. this should catch any regression quickly

infra-bot: deploy plan scheduled: console/frontend v3.2.7-canary -> rolling 10% prod in 15m. monitors attached: runtime-tests, workspace-mismatch-alert

jia: thanks all. followups: (1) add audit log entry for any preview response that contains mismatched workspace field, (2) run a one-off job to scan cache keys and invalidate v1 namespace

matt: logged followups in issue #872: audit + cache-scan job. good catch jia :thumbsup:

olivia: quick note: we should also review RBAC checks in the preview endpoint — caching is the obvious bug but defense-in-depth: endpoint should assert user has access to returned workspace before returning

jia: added server-side assert in PR too: if result.workspace !== requestedWorkspace -> log error + throw 403

sara: great. schedule postmortem doc? low-severity but customer-impacting if exploited. ping me with timeline tomorrow

jia: will write a short blameless notes doc and link the PR/tests. thanks everyone.
